chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We are in the mountain, so we send the shepherds with the sheep. Sometimes the sheep is injured or something strikes it, so they slaughter it, and we eat it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the slaughtered animal, and one does not rely upon it except from a Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: Is meat permissible if a shepherd slaughters an injured animal on behalf of the owner?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of the slaughter depends on the faith of the individual performing the act, ruling that meat is permissible if a Muslim shepherd slaughters an injured sheep in the owner's absence. This hadith highlights the Shia principle of 'amanah' (trustworthiness) in religious practice, where the Muslim's declaration of faith is sufficient to validate the ritual slaughter even if the owner is not present or known to be Muslim, distinguishing it from the stricter conditions often applied to the People of the Book.
